DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder

The polysomnography and REM sleep density analysis returned normal results, which helps rule out parasomnias like sleep terrors or obstructive sleep apnea. Since the untrusted input blocks have not provided the specific answers to your questions about memory recall and autonomic symptoms (sweating, rapid breathing), I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the clinical picture of an 8-year-old waking frightened with normal sleep architecture. Children with night terrors typically do not recall the event and have intense autonomic arousal, whereas those with nightmares recall the story and may have less intense physiological distress. The absence of abnormal sleep study findings combined with the history of "waking up frightened" strongly points to Nightmares rather than Night Terrors or Sleepwalking.
